artworks.title: Iphis and Ianthe
artworks.description: An Ovid plate titled for both brides: Iphis and Cretan Ianthe at the hinge of Metamorphoses IX. The print tradition is where Ianthe survives visually — the promised wife who loves a girl the gods will remake as a husband.

artworks.title: Iphis Transformed into a Young Man
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum RP-P-1886-A-10379: Isis answers Telethusa so that Iphis may wed Ianthe. The plate’s drama is the sex-change that clears the Cretan marriage — Ianthe present as the bride the metamorphosis is for.

artworks.title: Telethusa and Iphis Pray to Isis
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum RP-P-2014-34-55: mother and child before Isis — the prayer that will let Iphis stand beside Ianthe as husband. Part of the same Ovid cycle that carried the Cretan wedding into northern print shops.

artworks.title: Isis and Iphis
artworks.description: Baur’s Ovid illustration stages Isis transforming Iphis — the miracle that unlocks the marriage to Ianthe of Crete. Baroque line keeps the goddess’s gift as the visual climax of a myth rarely painted outside the Metamorphoses series.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses IX (Iphis and Ianthe)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid’s Cretan tale of Iphis and Ianthe — the girl raised as a boy, the bride who loves her, the goddess who changes the groom — is Ianthe’s sole lasting literary afterlife.
